title: Heat Pump Water Heater Rebate in Philadelphia 2026: PECO $350
desc: PECO pays $350 for an ENERGY STAR heat pump water heater in Philadelphia. Who it suits, basement and rowhouse tips, how to apply within 90 days.
lead: PECO pays Philadelphia homeowners $350 for an ENERGY STAR heat pump water heater. It is one of the larger PECO home rebates left in 2026. Here is who it suits, what a rowhouse basement needs, and how to claim it.
cards_heading: What water heater rebates pay in Philadelphia
cards_intro: The amount below comes from PECO's appliance rebate page, which we last read on September 29, 2026. It applies across the whole city.

cards.title: PECO heat pump water heater
cards.note: Must be ENERGY STAR certified and electric. Apply within 90 days of buying.

cards.title: Federal tax credit (25C)
cards.note: The federal credit for heat pump water heaters ended for spending after December 31, 2025.

after_cards:
How it works

A heat pump water heater pulls warmth out of the air around it and moves it into the tank. That takes much less power than heating water with a plain electric element. The $350 PECO rebate is paid after you buy, so you pay the full price first and get the money back once PECO approves your claim.
sections: Who should look at this in Philadelphia

This rebate fits best if your water heater is electric now. Swapping an old electric tank for a heat pump model cuts the power it uses, and every kilowatt-hour you save is on your PECO bill. The Census Bureau's American Community Survey (2020 to 2024) finds that 24.7% of Philadelphia households heat their homes with electricity, and many of those homes also heat water with it.

If your water heater runs on PGW gas, the math is harder. A heat pump model can still make sense when your gas tank is old and you want to move away from gas, but your savings will be smaller. Get a quote for both before you decide.

Most Philadelphia homes are old. The same Census survey shows 83.3% were built before 1980 and 39.9% before 1940, and 55.6% are rowhouses or twins. In many of these homes the water heater sits in a basement. That is often a good spot for a heat pump model, with some checks:

  • Space: the unit needs room around it to draw air. Small, closed-off closets can be too tight.
  • Drain: it makes water (condensate), so it needs a drain or a pump nearby.
  • Power: most need a 240-volt circuit, which an electric tank usually already has.
  • Cool air: it blows cooler air into the room. In a basement that also helps dry the air in summer.

Heat pump water heaters cost more than plain electric tanks up front. The $350 PECO rebate narrows that gap, and the lower power use does the rest over time. We don't publish a payback number for your home, because it depends on how much hot water your family uses and what your installer charges. Ask for a quote that shows the expected yearly energy use from the model's ENERGY STAR listing, then compare it with your current tank.
Plan the swap before the old tank fails

Most people replace a water heater the day it leaks. That rush pushes them into whatever plain tank the plumber has on the truck. A heat pump model can take a few days to order, so if your tank is ten years old or more, get a quote now. You will have time to check the space, line up the drain and pick an ENERGY STAR model that qualifies for the $350.
claim_heading: How to get the PECO water heater rebate
claim_steps: Confirm the model is ENERGY STAR certified. You can check on ENERGY STAR's product finder.
Buy and install it. A plumber is the usual choice; ask about the drain and the electrical circuit.
Keep the receipt and the model number.
Apply on PECO's rebate page within 90 days of the purchase.
faq: How much is the PECO water heater rebate?
$350 for an ENERGY STAR certified heat pump water heater.
Does PECO pay for a regular electric or gas water heater?
No. The rebate is for heat pump water heaters only.
How long do I have to apply?
PECO asks you to apply within 90 days of buying the water heater.
Is there still a federal tax credit for heat pump water heaters?
No. It ended for spending after December 31, 2025.
Can a heat pump water heater go in a small closet?
Sometimes, but many need more air than a closed closet gives. Check the maker's space rules, or ask about a louvered door or a ducted model.
